Tosafot on Bava Batra 153a:11:1.hebrew: לא כתב בה שכיב מרע כו' - וה"ה נמי דלא כתב בה לשון בריא, כדמהלך על רגלוהי בשוקא, אלא משום דקתני "צריך להביא ראיה שהוא שכיב מרע" נקט האי לישנא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 153a:11:1.english: "He did not write in it 'a person on his deathbed'..." - And the same law applies even if he did not write in it the language of a healthy person, such as "while walking on his feet in the marketplace." Rather, it is because [the Mishnah] teaches "he must bring proof that he was on his deathbed" that it used this phrasing.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 153a:12:1.hebrew: ולא כתב ביה מגו מרעיה איפטר לבית עולמיה - והיורשים היו טוענין שעמד, ואף על פי שלא היו טוענין שחזר בו — דודאי כיון שעמד, מסתמא ודאי חזר בו, אע"פ שלא אמר בפירוש. והכי משמע בגיטין פרק מי שאחזו (גיטין דף עב: ושם): דאמר רב הונא התם: גיטו כמתנתו; מה מתנתו, אם עמד — חוזר, אף גיטו חוזר. ופריך ליה מדתנן: "הרי זה גיטך מהיום אם מתי מחולי זה", והלך ועמד בשוק, וחלה ומת — אם מחמת החולי הראשון מת, הרי זה גט, ואם לאו, אינו גט. ואם אמרת אם עמד חוזר — הרי זה עמד! ומאי קושיא? דנהי דעמד, והלא לא חזר בו! אלא ש"מ דאפי' לא פירש שחזר בו, יש לנו לומר שחוזר בו. ועוד קאמר התם (דף עג.): א"ר אלעזר: שכיב מרע שניתק מחולי אל חולי — מתנתו מתנה. ודוקא ניתק, אבל עמד — אין מתנתו מתנה, אע"פ שלא חזר בו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 153a:12:1.english: "And he did not write in it, 'from his illness he passed away to his eternal home'" - And the heirs were claiming that he got up [i.e., recovered], even though they were not claiming that he retracted [the gift] — for certainly, since he got up, presumably he certainly retracted, even though he did not say so explicitly. And so it implies in Gittin, in the chapter "Mi She'achazo" (Gittin 72b, and there): For Rav Huna said there: His bill of divorce is like his gift; just as with his gift, if he got up [from his illness] he retracts, so too his bill of divorce is retracted. And [the Gemara] challenges him from what we learned: "This is your bill of divorce from today if I die from this illness," and he went and stood in the marketplace, and then fell ill and died — if he died from the first illness, it is a valid bill of divorce, and if not, it is not a bill of divorce. But if you say that if he got up he retracts — behold, he got up! And what is the difficulty? Granted that he got up, but he did not retract! Rather, learn from this that even if he did not explicitly state that he retracted, we should say that he retracts. And furthermore, it says there (73a): Rabbi Elazar said: A person on his deathbed who shifted from one illness to another — his gift is a valid gift. And only if he shifted [to another illness], but if he got up [recovered], his gift is not a valid gift, even though he did not retract.
